question.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $t(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x$ and $v(x)={e}^{x}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{t}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)^{′}\cdot {e}^{x}-\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\cdot ({e}^{x})^{′}}{({e}^{x})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{{e}^{2x}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}(\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)}{{e}^{2x}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{{e}^{x}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
